config.caFile.description: Path to a PEM file holding the certificate authority that signed the deployment's TLS certificate, for a deployment behind a private CA. Trusted in addition to the system's authorities. Empty uses the system's authorities alone.
config.commitMessageStyle.markdownDescri: How **Generate Commit Message** writes a message: a convention (Conventional Commits, a ticket prefix) or plain words. Empty uses a summary line of at most 72 characters in the imperative mood, a blank line, and a short body saying what changed and why. A workspace can set its own.
config.showAnswerUsage.description: Show under each answer the tokens it used and their cost at the model's list price.

walkthrough.gettingStarted.title: Get started with MatterWave
walkthrough.gettingStarted.description: Sign in, ask about your code, and let MatterWave change it under review.
walkthrough.gettingStarted.signIn.title: Sign in
walkthrough.gettingStarted.signIn.descri:
Confirm a code in your browser, or paste an API key. The credential stays in the editor's secret storage.
[Sign In](command:matterwave.signInWithDeviceCode)
walkthrough.gettingStarted.askAboutSelec:
Select some code and ask about it; the answer streams into the chat view.
[Ask about Selection](command:matterwave.askAboutSelection)
walkthrough.gettingStarted.apply.title: Apply an answer's code
walkthrough.gettingStarted.apply.descrip:
Every code block in an answer has Apply. A diff opens first, and the change lands in the editor, where Undo takes it back.
[Open Chat](command:matterwave.openChat)
walkthrough.gettingStarted.inlineEdit.de:
Select lines, say what should change, and review the diff before it lands.
[Edit Selection](command:matterwave.inlineEdit)
capabilities.untrustedWorkspaces.descrip: In Restricted Mode MatterWave chats and reads context, but does not change files (Apply, inline edit, Restore Checkpoint) or run git for @git, and the coding agent (its file and shell tools, MATTERWAVE.md, project commands, subagents and MCP servers) stays off, until the workspace is trusted.
config.agent.defaultMode.description: The agent's approval mode in a new workspace. Yolo (nothing asks) is not a default: it is allowed per session, from the mode chip, /approval-mode or Shift+Tab, after a confirm. A workspace's settings can make this stricter (plan), never looser.
config.agent.defaultMode.plan: Read and search only: no file changes, no commands.
config.agent.defaultMode.ask: Every file change and every command needs your approval (the default).
config.agent.defaultMode.autoEdit: File changes are applied without asking (a change to the agent's or the editor's own settings still asks); commands still ask.
config.agent.maxSteps.description: The most model calls one agent run makes before it stops and says so. A workspace's settings can lower it, not raise it past yours.
config.agent.maxTokens.description: The most tokens one agent run spends (prompt and completion, every step) before it stops and says so. A workspace's settings can lower it, not raise it past yours.
config.agent.editorContext.description: Send the active file's name, the selection (up to 8,000 characters) and the recently opened files' names with each agent prompt. Files the deny list covers are never sent.
config.agent.webFetch.description: Offer the agent web_fetch. Every fetch asks first in the ask and auto-edit modes; plan does not offer it.
config.agent.matterwaveMcp.description: Offer the agent MatterWave's own MCP server (/mcp on matterwave.baseUrl, signed in as this editor): your conversations and models as tools.
config.agent.mcpServers.markdownDescript: MCP servers the agent may use, by name. Each is `{ "command": "...", "args": [...], "env": {...} }` (stdio) or `{ "url": "https://...", "headers": {...} }` (HTTP), with an optional `"tools": [...]` allow-list (only those tools reach the model), `"trust": true` (your standing approval: its tools run without asking where they would ask) and `"disabled": true`. Every other MCP tool asks before each call outside yolo. Workspace settings apply only in a trusted folder, and each server they add asks before it first starts (again whenever its definition changes); `trust` counts only in your user settings. A server's read-only marks, which let plan mode offer a tool (still asking), are believed only for a trusted server and MatterWave's own.
